correctness.rationale: Translation reduces the problem to \(\{0,a,b\}\). The determinant identity is exact. The proof handles separately the cases \(N\mid ab\) and \(N\nmid ab\); in the latter case the phase identity forces \(N\mid(b-a)^2\) and then the determinant becomes \(-X(R-1)^2\), giving the missing cross-divisibility condition. The order-coset and \(p\)-adic forms are algebraically equivalent. The packaged cyclotomic verifier checks every normalized triple for \(3\le N\le120\), but the infinite result rests on the symbolic proof rather than enumeration.

originality.rationale: The closest full-text source, Caragea--Lee arXiv:2409.09793, proves the global square-free nonvanishing theorem and nonsquare-free existence theorem. Prime-order all-minor results of Tao and Frenkel are strictly narrower in modulus. Targeted searches for equivalent local formulations found no matching statement.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification at the first nontrivial principal-minor size beyond pairs. It refines a global existence/nonexistence theorem into an exact local arithmetic test and exposes a square-divisor/additive-order mechanism. The criterion can filter or count singular triples without determinant evaluation and clarifies why nonsquare-free moduli contain both singular and nonsingular triples.
